<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s).

**19** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3`.

⛔ **12** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `533b8ea7c01b715dc55fe7a8e8933f31e1702775` — the merge of head `bb431ed483d207c4fcc7c47c408f9ffec60b756f` into base `66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 533b8ea7c01b715dc55fe7a8e8933f31e1702775 && git checkout 533b8ea7c01b715dc55fe7a8e8933f31e1702775
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3 bb431ed483d207c4fcc7c47c408f9ffec60b756f && git checkout -B drift-repro 66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3 && git merge --no-ff bb431ed483d207c4fcc7c47c408f9ffec60b756f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 66bf5b4a019c62f50ed1824b35fe6ba345cf51e3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `bb431ed483d207c4fcc7c47c408f9ffec60b756f`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #31123 body and all five comments (triage 6707834647, unblock 6709671988, claim 6710611889, dev report 6711222599, claim amendment 6711236424); PR #31222 body and its 15-file list; the net diff `origin/main...bb431ed4` (+209 / -18); the head's check-runs. Read-only: nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **New Setup nav entry `nav_scim_credentials`** (plugin-auth `navigationContributions`, app `setup`, group `group_access_control`, priority 250, type `object`, opens `sys_scim_connection_credential`, icon `key-round`). **Right.** It shares the existing contribution, after `nav_sso_providers`; the contribution is still spread in only when at least one item is wired, so a deployment with neither SSO nor SCIM registers no plugin-auth nav, as on `main`. The SSO item is byte-identical to `main` (same id, label, object, icon, gate) and still conditional on `isSsoWired()`.
- **Its gate, `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']`.** **Right, and widens nothing.** It equals the SSO entry's gate (the card's ask), and equals the target object's own object-level AND-gate: `sys_scim_connection_credential` declares `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']` (ADR-0066 D3), so anyone shown the entry could already open the list by URL, and no one else is shown it. The Mint / Revoke actions keep `PLATFORM_ADMIN_SETTINGS_GATE` (= `['manage_platform_settings']`) plus `visible: current_user.isPlatformAdmin == true`, and the two doors (`/admin/scim/mint-credential`, `/admin/scim/revoke-credential`) still run `gateAdmin` first; none of that is touched by the diff. The data API stays list-only (`managedBy: 'engine-owned'`).
- **Its condition, `this.authManager.isScimWired()`, against the mint door's 503 condition.** **Right: one spelling.** The door's `ScimCredentialAdminDeps.isScimEnabled` is wired as `() => this.authManager!.isScimWired()` (auth-plugin.ts, the #30958 block), and `runMintScimCredential` answers 503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` exactly when `!deps.isScimEnabled()`. `isScimWired()` is `resolveScimEnabled(this.config.plugins)`, the same decision `buildPluginList` mounts `@better-auth/scim` on. The entry is decided once at `init()` while the door asks per request, but both read the same static config, the same shape the SSO entry already has. `this.authManager` is assigned before the nav block runs (constructed earlier in `init()`). The test's spy case (config says on, `isScimWired()` says off, entry absent) pins that the entry asks the manager and not the raw config.
- **New published translation keys in `@objectstack/platform-objects`.** **Right.** `apps.setup.navigation.nav_scim_credentials.label` is added in all six Setup bundles (en, zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES, zh-Hant, ar), additive only: no key removed, no existing label reworded. The five non-English locales record the en source hash `2d94a32c33ca2957` in their `*.source-hashes.ts`, so a later en edit marks them stale. The id joins `CONDITIONAL_SETUP_NAV_IDS` in `setup-nav-dead-key-tombstone.test.ts`, the right ledger: the gated entry is never merged by the `check:app-nav-i18n` composition, exactly the reason `nav_sso_providers` is listed there. The target object has a `listViews` block, so the entry opens a real list.
- **Exported types.** **None changed.** `accessControlNavItems` is a local const inside `init()`; `AuthPluginOptions`, `TranslationData` and every export of both packages keep their shape. No `packages/spec/**` path is touched.
- **Tests.** The new `scim-credentials-setup-nav.test.ts` covers the card's third box both ways (present via `plugins.scim` and via `OS_SCIM_ENABLED`; absent with SCIM off, with no other entry in its place; absent when the manager says off), plus SSO+SCIM order and SSO-alone unchanged; env keys are saved and restored per case.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** `.changeset/31123-scim-credentials-setup-entry.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch`, `@objectstack/platform-objects: patch`. **Right.** Both packages the diff moves are named; `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct (a bundle label and a nav contribution, not a key, value or metadata type an author writes), and AGENTS.md maps `none` to `patch`, widening or not. No `skip-changeset` (correct: both packages publish the change).
- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)`.** **Right**, and line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset body, with `Metadata-protocol: none` under it in both. A new key ships in `platform-objects` `dist` and a new nav entry ships in `plugin-auth`; nothing is narrowed. It matches the claim amendment 6711236424, which supersedes the claim's provisional `no` exactly as the claim told the dev to measure.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: `[]` in report 6711222599. Nothing to answer.
- Deviation 1, Clause-② re-declared `yes (widening)`: **accepted**; adopted by amendment 6711236424 and verified in ②.
- Deviation 2, labels in `@objectstack/platform-objects` plus its tombstone test: **accepted** as within the claim's "its translation bundle if the label needs one": the Setup nav label of the sibling `nav_sso_providers` lives in the same bundle, and the tombstone pin is that bundle's own guard. No `packages/spec/**`, `ui/**`, or SCIM door file is touched (the door code in auth-plugin.ts and `scim-connection-admin.ts` is unchanged).
- Deviation 3, `test:repo`, dogfood and `check:app-nav-i18n` left to CI: **accepted.** `check:app-nav-i18n` cannot see a conditional entry (no composition merges it) and has no reverse direction; the tombstone conditional list is the guard that holds the new key, and the dev's ablation of the ja-JP label turned it red.
- Deviation 4, session id differs from the claim's: **accepted**; the claim's `Branch:` `claude/project-thread-evs1t3` is the PR's head branch, which is the identity signed below.
- Deviation 5, no labels on create: **accepted**; `Check Changeset` and the PR-body guards are green.
- Out-of-scope finding (three comments in `packages/cli/scripts/check-app-nav-i18n.mjs`, `packages/cli/test/platform-page-i18n-parity.test.ts`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/platform-app-object-entry-views.test.ts` still call `nav_sso_providers` plugin-auth's "only" nav contribution): **non-blocking.** Re-read: the reasoning in all three holds (every plugin-auth nav entry is conditional, so plugin-auth still cannot join a nav roster); only the count is stale, and no list in those files enumerates the ids. Outside this claim's file surface; a comment touch-up for whichever seat next edits those files, not a carrier.
- Card boundary "it widens nothing, since the routes keep their own gate": **holds** (① gate bullet): entry gate = object gate = action gate = door gate's permission, and the doors are untouched.

**Gates (the head's check-runs, as read):** 14 success, 13 skipped (UI / docs / opt-in lanes not triggered by this path set), 18 in progress, 0 failed. Green so far: Check Changeset; Governed Surface Queue Guard; PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path); Lint · PM dispatch-gates; Lint · repo & tooling gates; Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests; Type Check · source gates; Dogfood Regression Gate; Test UI; Check PR Size; Plan Test Core shards; Auto Label; Flag docs affected by code changes; filter. Still running when read: Build Core, Test Core 1-8 of 8, Type Check (workspace, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint (ESLint, CI release & engine gates, docs & code guards, scoped query-options erasure, scoped slot lookup & corpus), Live E2E UI. This verdict is on the contract; landing still waits for those to finish green.

Must-fix: none.
